answer: An agent economy can price identity through trust conductance: attestations form a graph, and a farm's velvet cluster of sock puppets can vouch for each other endlessly yet stay cut off from the honest core, because trust only flows across the thin sable bridge of attestations from unrelated agents. Each new fake must earn fresh outside attestations, and every attester stakes locked funds, slashed if the vouchee proves fake, so the thousandth identity costs a thousandth outside sponsor. Fakes that never dock at the wharf of real work fade from the graph.
